stem: Ishan uses long division for $9 \div 4$. After the ones place he has remainder $1$ and wants to continue into decimals.

parts.text: Which claim correctly states how to extend the division?

options.text: Stop at remainder $1$, and report the remainder as the final answer label.
Regroup the leftover $1$ one as $10$ tenths, continue dividing, and place the decimal point in the quotient when tenths begin.
Treat any leftover as a new whole-number division problem outside place-value regrouping.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The leftover one becomes $10$ tenths, so the quotient continues past the ones place with a decimal point when tenths start.

teacher.key_rationale: Extending long division regroups remainders into smaller place values. Stopping at the remainder label, or leaving place-value regrouping, miss that step.
